items.title: Execute typed SQL function query programs
items.body:
## Why

SQL-language functions retained their full body text but only admitted and ran one plain `SELECT`. A valid multi-query body therefore either failed at creation or made its final result unreachable; a top-level set operation was incorrectly classified as a non-query.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| A function body was limited to one ordinary `SELECT` | A typed program represents one or more read-only ordinary or set-operation queries |
| Leading queries could not run | Every query runs in order; only the final query supplies the function result |
| `UNION` / `INTERSECT` / `EXCEPT` bodies were rejected as non-query statements | Set operations preserve CTE, ordering, limit, spill, and composite-result semantics through an internal row-source boundary |
| Scalar and table-function paths independently reparsed one statement | Both consume the same typed program and preserve their distinct scalar/table result contracts |

## Evidence

Regression coverage exercises suppressed leading set results, propagated leading-query errors, final CTE-backed set results, table-function output, lifecycle validation, and PostgreSQL differential comparison.

items.title: 🐛 fix benchmark submit gateway url and results rendering
items.body:
## Summary

Five defects in the benchmark feature (PACT-756, https://linear.app/pact-toolkit/issue/PACT-756), plus a mock-data fix to keep the mock experience consistent with the real contract:

1. **Gateway URL fallback** - `BenchmarkWorkbench.tsx` fell back to `http://localhost:8080` (pact-auth's port) when `NEXT_PUBLIC_PACT_GATEWAY_URL` was unset, instead of the gateway's `:8110`. This is why a real 180-row run against a real backend errored on every single row. Fallback corrected to `:8110`. Audited every file under `env/`:
   - `env/local-real.env`: added `NEXT_PUBLIC_PACT_GATEWAY_URL=http://localhost:8110` right after the existing `PACT_GATEWAY_URL` line (matches the value already in that file).
   - `env/demo.env`: added `NEXT_PUBLIC_PACT_GATEWAY_URL` matching its existing `PACT_GATEWAY_URL` (`https://api-demo.pact.example.com`).
   - `env/local.env`: corrected the stale `PACT_GATEWAY_URL=http://localhost:8080` to `:8110`. Did **not** add `NEXT_PUBLIC_PACT_GATEWAY_URL` here - `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_MOCKING=enabled` means MSW intercepts every request in this env, so the client-side gateway URL is never read.

2. **isRowCorrect label mismatch** - compared `expected_label` against `'hostile'`/`'safe'`, but the gateway/pact-benchmark contract (verified against `pact-benchmark`'s `runner/corpus.py` and `runner/runner.py`) only ever produces lowercase `'allow'`/`'block'`. Every real-backend row was silently marked incorrect. Fixed to compare against the real contract values. The generated `BenchmarkJobRowBody.expected_label` type is a plain `string` (not a narrowed union), so no codegen type needed changing.

3. **Client corpus validation** - `validateCorpusFile` checked column presence but never validated label values. Added value validation (case-insensitive, matching the backend's lowercase-then-check behavior in `corpus.py`) across every row, not just the first. On violation, the error names the offending row number and the bad value, e.g. `Row 3: expected_label must be "allow" or "block", got "hostile"`.

4. **Per-row error rendering** - the results table rendered an "error" chip for the Decision column but never the row's `error` message string, making failed rows undiagnosable from the UI. Added a quiet (`text-xs text-muted-foreground`), truncated `Error` column with a `title` tooltip carrying the full message; empty when the row has no error.

5. **Run-comparison select overflow** - long run labels overflowed the Baseline/Candidate `<select>` elements horizontally out of the card. Added `min-w-0` to the flex parents and `max-w-full truncate` to both selects so long labels ellipsize inside the card instead of overflowing it.

6. **Mock data followed the old vocabulary** - `MOCK_ROWS` in `src/app/benchmark/mock/data/benchmark.ts` seeded `expected_label` as `hostile`/`safe`, the same wrong vocabulary `isRowCorrect` used to compare against. Once #2 above fixed `isRowCorrect` to check the real `allow`/`block` contract, every mock-mode row started rendering "Incorrect" (previously masked because both sides agreed on the wrong vocabulary). Reseeded `MOCK_ROWS` to `allow`/`block` (safe -> allow, hostile -> block), keeping the same correct/incorrect row pattern (every 7th row deliberately wrong) so the Correct column shows a realistic mix again.

## Verification

**Gates** (from a fresh clone, branch off master, re-run after the mock-data commit):
- `tsc --noEmit` - pass
- `eslint .` - pass
- `TZ=CET vitest run` - 626 tests passed (77 files), including 15 new tests in `src/app/benchmark/test/benchmark_job.test.ts` covering the isRowCorrect allow/block/error matrix and validateCorpusFile's bad-label-value/case-insensitivity/valid-file paths for both JSONL and CSV
- `next build` - pass

**Mock-mode E2E** (`env/local.env` via `PORT=3910 pnpm run dev:mock`, driven with a throwaway Playwright script, deleted afterward):
- `/benchmark` loaded cleanly, no console errors
- Run comparison card: with the seeded mock run labels (e.g. `stub · seed-v2.jsonl · v0.5.0 · 22 Jul 2026`), `document.body.scrollWidth` equaled `window.innerWidth` (1280px) - no horizontal overflow, confirmed by screenshot
- Submitted a corpus through the upload form; the mock job progressed to done and the per-row results table rendered with the new `Error` column present in the header, `Expected`/`Decision` values as `allow`/`block`, and the Correct column showing a realistic mix (17 correct / 3 incorrect across the first page of 20 rows) instead of all-incorrect

items.title: Results navigation, incorrect-only review, and a distinct marked colour
items.body:
## Summary

Three fixes to reviewing a graded block, plus a toolbar tidy-up.

**Marked-for-review and incorrect were the same colour.** `--marked` and `--incorrect` were both `#c0392b`, so the two legend dots were pixel-identical — and an item can be both marked *and* incorrect at once, so they must never read as one signal. Marked is now violet `#6b3fa0`, which also stays separable from the red/green pair under the common forms of colour blindness. The corner dot gains a white ring so it stays legible on the tinted correct and incorrect cells.

**There was no way back to the results screen.** `End Block & See Results` is hidden once graded, so leaving Exam Complete — via `Back to Exam` or by clicking a results row — stranded you in the question list with no route back. The Pause slot sits unused once graded, so it now holds a **Results** button, and the item review overlay gains **Back to Results**.

**Reviewing only your misses took a round trip through the results table per item.** The overlay now offers **Go to first incorrect**, and the bottom bar a **Next incorrect (n)** button that steps through them in order and wraps at the end. Both treat unanswered items as incorrect, since those are equally worth reviewing.

Also: **Lab Values is hidden on the results screen**, and the panel closes if it is open when the block is graded — the split layout has no question to sit beside there.

## Verification

96 automated browser checks across five suites, all passing with no console errors. New coverage:

- the four status colours are mutually distinct
- Results / Next incorrect / Back to Results / Go to first incorrect are absent before grading and present after
- Results button round-trips to Exam Complete from both the question view and the review overlay, with the score card intact
- every `Next incorrect` landing is genuinely an incorrect item, order ascends, and it wraps from the last back to the first
- the count in the button label matches the real number of wrong answers
- Lab Values hides on results, reappears on `Back to Exam`, and an open panel is closed on grading — including on a reload straight into a graded exam

Two older assertions were updated for intent rather than count: the toolbar icon test (now 5 icons) and the bottom-bar test, which now counts *visible* buttons so the hidden `Next incorrect` does not trip it.

items.title: Fix AR invoice unit price calculation, date extraction, and pipeline results display
items.body:
AR invoices were submitted to Oracle with inflated amounts (subtotal passed as unit price), the date column lookup was brittle against export format variants, and the pipeline UI showed no per-invoice outcome after batch creation.

## Amount calculation
`UnitSellingPrice` was incorrectly set to `Order Lines/Subtotal w/o Tax` (line total), causing Oracle to multiply again by quantity. Now correctly computes:

```
UnitSellingPrice = Subtotal w/o Tax ÷ Base Quantity
```

Added `Order Lines/Tax Excl.` / `Order Lines/Tax Excl` (YASMEEN format) to subtotal aliases. Falls back to direct unit-price columns (no division) if no subtotal column is present. Division-by-zero guarded.

## Date column aliases
Extended date detection to cover additional export variants: `Order Lines/Date`, `Order Date`, `Sale Date`, `Transaction Date`, `Order Lines/Transaction Date`, alongside existing aliases.

## Per-invoice pipeline results
`getInvoiceBatchProgress` now queries `ArInvoiceUpload` records on completion and returns an `invoiceResults` array — customer name, transaction date, Oracle `TransactionNumber`, status, and error message per invoice.

The pipeline page renders a full results table after batch creation instead of the previous summary-only message, with links to individual upload detail pages.

items.title: feat(datasource): switch search to /api/v3/trace-summaries (ADR-010)
items.body:
## Summary

Switches the datasource search query from the legacy \`GET /api/traces\` (v1) to the new \`GET /api/v3/trace-summaries\` endpoint introduced in [ADR-010](https://github.com/jaegertracing/jaeger/blob/main/docs/adr/010-trace-summary-api.md) (Milestones 1–4 complete).

**Why:** The v1 endpoint returns full span payloads for every matching trace; the UI then post-processed them client-side to extract summary fields. The v3 endpoint returns pre-aggregated \`TraceSummary\` objects server-side, eliminating the span payload entirely.

**New fields in the results table:**
| Field | Notes |
|-------|-------|
| \`traceID\` | Hex trace ID, links to trace detail |
| \`traceName\` | \`rootService: rootOperation\` |
| \`startTime\` | Absolute start time of the earliest span |
| \`duration\` | Accurate wall-clock duration: \`maxEndTime − minStartTime\` (µs) |
| \`spanCount\` | Total spans in the trace |
| \`errorCount\` | Spans with OTEL \`StatusCode=ERROR\` |
| \`services\` | Per-service breakdown: \`frontend(12) backend(30,⚠2)\` |

The old \`duration\` was incorrect — it used root span duration, not trace wall-clock time.

**Query parameter mapping (v1 → v3):**
| v1 | v3 |
|----|----|
| \`service=X\` | \`query.serviceName=X\` |
| \`start=<µs>\` | \`query.startTimeMin=<RFC3339>\` |
| \`end=<µs>\` | \`query.startTimeMax=<RFC3339>\` |
| \`operation=X\` | \`query.operationName=X\` |
| \`limit=N\` | \`query.searchDepth=N\` |
| \`minDuration=X\` | \`query.durationMin=X\` |
| \`maxDuration=X\` | \`query.durationMax=X\` |
| \`tag=key:value\` | \`query.attributes={"key":"value"}\` (JSON map) |

**Tag format:** logfmt (\`key=value\` pairs, quoted values supported), matching Jaeger UI. Example: \`error=true db.statement="select * from User"\`

**Timestamp precision:** Unix nanosecond strings are truncated to µs in string space before parsing to avoid \`Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER\` precision loss.

**docker-compose overrides:** \`JAEGER_IMAGE\` and \`HOTROD_IMAGE\` accept a full image reference (digest-pinned by default). Override for snapshot testing:
\`\`\`bash
JAEGER_IMAGE=jaegertracing/jaeger-snapshot:latest make server
\`\`\`

## Test plan

Covered by CI:
- Unit tests: \`npm run test:ci --workspace=packages/datasource\` (14 tests)
- E2e test in \`tests/panel.spec.ts\`: runs a search against the live HotROD stack and asserts the results table contains all expected columns with at least one data row

items.title: Fix graded-mode navigation and hide controls that do not apply
items.body:
## The reported bug

"Go to first incorrect" did nothing. It set the item and re-rendered — but the results screen was still on top, so the render happened *underneath* it and nothing visibly changed.

It was not one button. **Every item-navigation path reachable from the review overlay while Exam Complete was showing had the same defect:** the item grid and "Go to first unanswered" were equally dead, and the top bar's Previous/Next silently moved a question the user could not see. Only two paths (the results table row and "Back to Exam") happened to swap the view first.

All navigation now goes through a single `goToItem()` that leaves the results screen before rendering, so an item click always ends with that item on screen regardless of where it was triggered.

## The rest of the graded-mode audit

- **The item counter, Previous/Next and the entire subbar are hidden on the results screen.** They describe the current question and there is none. The subbar was actively misleading: its "Mark for review" checkbox flagged the hidden current item, and its answered count went stale the moment the block was graded (still reading "50 of 50 answered" beside a finished score).
- **The results filter is remembered.** Stepping out to an item and back no longer drops you from "Incorrect" to the full list every time — which was precisely the workflow of reviewing your misses one at a time. Restart clears it.
- **A filter matching nothing says so**, instead of leaving an empty table under a header row that reads as a glitch.
- **Results rows are real controls** — focusable, operable with Enter or Space, and labelled for screen readers. They were click-only.
- **The downloaded .txt carries the form label and time on block**, matching what the score card shows.
- **On the last item once graded**, the footer button reads "Item List" rather than "Review / Finish" — there is nothing left to finish.

## Verification

127 automated browser checks across six suites, all passing with no console errors. The new suite drives graded mode specifically:

- all four navigation entry points (first-incorrect, item grid, results row, keyboard on a row) leave the results screen *and* land on the right item
- inert chrome is absent on results and returns in the question view, with the answered note refreshed to the score
- the filter survives a round trip with the correct chip still active; the empty state appears and clears; restart resets it
- the download contains score, time, form label, and all 50 items

items.title: fix: enforce Gaijin Market price cap
items.body:
## Summary

* Add immutable and versioned Gaijin Market rules
* Enforce the 2000.00 GJN maximum listing price
* Derive the 1700.00 GJN maximum seller settlement proceeds
* Exclude over-cap prices from market analysis
* Add capped and tri-state break-even behavior
* Add theoretical maximum net-profit calculation
* Return market-rule metadata through the analysis API
* Display price-cap behavior in the item analysis panel
* Reject stale API response contracts instead of displaying misleading fallback results
* Fix analysis requests under React StrictMode and URL navigation
* Add a future-development log for strength assessments, return events, and community feedback

## Market rules

The analytics package now uses immutable Gaijin Market rules:

* Maximum listing price: `2000.00 GJN`
* Nominal fee rate: `15%`
* Currency quantum: `0.01 GJN`
* Seller proceeds are rounded down to `0.01 GJN`
* Maximum seller settlement proceeds: `1700.00 GJN`

The maximum seller proceeds are derived from the listing cap and the fixed fee policy rather than stored as a separate hard-coded value.

## Price validation

A valid Gaijin Market price must satisfy:

```text
0 < price <= 2000.00 GJN
```

Prices above the cap:

* Are not clamped to 2000
* Are excluded from current-price, median, volatility, and reference-price calculations
* Produce the stable `price_above_market_cap` reason code
* Do not necessarily prevent analysis when other valid observations remain

## Break-even behavior

Break-even reachability uses three states:

* `true`: a legal listing price at or below 2000.00 GJN can recover the purchase price
* `false`: the required listing price exceeds the market cap
* `null`: there is not enough valid information to calculate reachability

Verified live examples:

```text
Buy price: 1700.00 GJN
Break-even listing price: 2000.00 GJN
Break-even reachable: true
Maximum net profit: 0.00 GJN
```

```text
Buy price: 1700.01 GJN
Break-even listing price: null
Break-even reachable: false
Maximum net profit: -0.01 GJN
Reason: break_even_unreachable_under_market_cap
```

The implementation never clamps an unreachable break-even result to a misleading 2000.00 GJN value.

## API response

The analysis response now includes immutable market-rule metadata:

* Rule name and version
* Maximum listing price
* Maximum seller settlement proceeds
* Currency quantum

Analysis output includes:

* `maximum_net_profit`
* `break_even_sell_price`
* `break_even_reachable`

All Decimal values remain JSON strings or null.

The analysis route still accepts only:

* `item_id`
* `horizon`
* Optional `as_of`

Users cannot configure the fee policy, market cap, or market-rule version.

## Web runtime fixes

Manual browser smoke testing exposed two frontend issues.

### React StrictMode auto-run

The previous auto-run implementation recorded its deduplication key before the request actually started. In development StrictMode, the first effect cleanup cancelled the scheduled request, while the second effect was incorrectly blocked as a duplicate.

The updated implementation only deduplicates requests in a way that remains correct during StrictMode effect setup and cleanup.

### URL navigation and request cancellation

Manual submission previously updated the URL and started a request at the same time. Navigation could unmount or replace the component and abort that request, while the StrictMode deduplication bug prevented the URL-driven request from replacing it.

The URL is now the committed source of analysis state, and the URL-driven auto-run starts the request.

A single user action now produces one analysis API request.

## API contract compatibility

The frontend no longer fills missing new-contract fields with default market rules and then displays old API calculations.

A stale API response could previously produce contradictory output such as:

```text
Maximum listing price: 2000.00 GJN
Break-even listing price: 2000.02 GJN
```

The frontend now validates the analysis response contract before rendering calculated results.

When the API response is missing required current-contract fields, the panel:

* Ends the loading state
* Clears stale analysis results
* Does not display old calculations
* Shows a stable API-version incompatibility message
* Does not expose internal stack traces or field names

Displayed message:

```text
分析服务版本与当前网页不兼容，请重启或更新API后重试。
```

## Web behavior

The analysis panel displays:

* Highest legal listing price
* Highest seller settlement proceeds
* Theoretical maximum net profit at the current purchase price
* Reachable, unreachable, and unavailable break-even states

The interface does not describe 1700.00 GJN as a universal profit limit or guaranteed return.

## Future development log

The new planning document records—but does not implement:

* Administrator strength assessments
* Strength-change events
* Return and supply-shock event tracking
* Shadow-mode evaluation
* Future RuleBasedV2 research
* Community feedback with administrator approval
* Abuse-prevention requirements

No administrator database, event database, community rating system, scraper, machine-learning model, or RuleBasedV2 implementation is included.

## Live verification

The active local API process was restarted from the current working tree.

Live API results:

* Reachable item: HTTP 200, 73 ms
* Unreachable item: HTTP 200, 12 ms
* Ordinary insufficient-data item: HTTP 200, 12 ms

The unreachable result returned:

```json
{
  "maximum_net_profit": "-0.01",
  "break_even_sell_price": null,
  "break_even_reachable": false
}
```

It no longer returned the stale pre-cap value `2000.02`.

Browser verification confirmed:

* One click produced one analysis API request
* Loading completed normally
* No React error page
* No stale-event `currentTarget` error
* Reachable, unreachable, and insufficient-data states rendered correctly
* URL refresh restored analysis at most once
* No horizontal overflow at 390px width

The two market-cap test products were created from two distinct item keys and were not an import defect.

## Validation

* Analytics compile check: passed
* Analytics tests: 72 passed
* API compile check: passed
* API tests: 106 passed
* OpenAPI contract check: passed
* Web tests: 51 passed
* Web lint: passed
* Web typecheck: passed
* Web production build: passed
* Docker Compose config: passed
* Migration check: no changes
* `analysis_results` table check: not created
* Sensitive-information scan: passed
* `git diff --check`: passed
* Live API smoke test: passed
* Desktop browser smoke test: passed
* 390px browser smoke test: passed

## Known non-blocking warnings

* Local Node version is 24.14.0 while the project declares Node 22.x
* Existing Node module-type warnings
* Existing Starlette/httpx test deprecation warning
* Docker configuration access warning
* Git CRLF normalization warnings

## Database

This pull request:

* Adds no Alembic migration
* Adds no `analysis_results` table
* Does not persist analysis results
* Does not add administrator, event, or community-feedback tables

Temporary synthetic smoke-test data was removed after verification.

## Scope

This pull request does not:

items.title: Clinical correlates: large-clone analyses, age/BMI, survival — and a metadata repair
items.body:
Finishes the outstanding analyses from my notes: Fairfax-inspired large-clone
comparisons, age/BMI covariates, and PFS/OS modelling. Adds
`NRG-GY003_TCR_TRB_Clinical_Correlates.qmd` plus `R/clinical_repertoire.R` for
shared setup, so documents share one definition of the clinical join and the
repertoire metrics.

Clinical data (OS and censoring indicators, which the repertoire metadata lacks)
come from the companion WES project. All 90 TRB patients have clinical data.

## Findings

- **Large clones track clinical benefit.** CB patients hold more of their
  baseline repertoire in large clones (14.0% vs 7.8%, p=0.027) and have higher
  clonality (p=0.037). Repertoire *size* measures show nothing. Adjusted for
  molecular depth via a negative-binomial offset, CB carries a **1.65× higher
  rate of large clones (p=0.032)**, unchanged by age, BMI or treatment arm.
- **The discriminating clone size is ~3.7% of the repertoire, not 0.5%** — an
  order of magnitude above the melanoma cutoff; 0.5% is not significant here
  (p=0.066). The sweep scans 60 correlated thresholds, so it is reported with BH
  correction (p=0.039) and a label-permutation null (global p=0.014).
- **Age and BMI: clean null.** No association with response or any repertoire
  metric.
- **No baseline metric predicts PFS or OS**, at any cutoff tested.

## Two things a reviewer should look at

**1. `immunarch`'s `Clones` is a read count, not a cell count.** These libraries
carry UMIs. Molecular depth varies ~800-fold while read depth is near-constant by
design, so read-derived proportions assume a uniform sampling that does not hold.
Observed richness tracks UMI depth at rho=0.89. `load_umi_repertoires()` reads
the UMI counts directly, and depth enters the models explicitly.

A consequence: the README claim that *"tumor samples show fewer unique clonotypes
but higher absolute clone counts"* is what low-complexity libraries sequenced
deeply look like (tumours have 6.5× fewer molecules but ~2× more reads), not
biology. **I have deliberately left the README unchanged** — that is a stated
conclusion and yours to revise.

**2. The tumour-resident finding was re-tested and survives.** CB tumours were
sampled ~2.5× more deeply than NCB (p=0.044) and tumour-resident fraction tracks
tumour depth (rho=0.44), so the unadjusted result was at risk of being an
artefact. Adjusted for tumour and blood depth, the response effect holds
(p=0.038) while depth itself drops out (p=0.14). Rests on 37 patients.

## Metadata repair, and its cause

77 of 228 TRB rows and 75 of 226 TRA rows in `All_Samples/metadata.txt` were
column-shifted: an unlabelled age-bin value inserted after `Age` pushed `BMI`,
`PFS`, `Response`, `Response_SD` and `Tumor_T_cells` one column right.

The cause was `input/TRA/Nivo_NCB_TRA/metadata.txt`, the only file declaring a
14th column `AgeCut`; concatenating the per-arm files into `All_Samples` carried
those values but not the header.

It hid from a column-count check because clean rows carry a trailing tab and
shifted rows do not, so every line split into 14 fields either way. The symptom
was `Response` holding a mix of `CB`/`NCB` and numbers like `1.91`, and
`Tumor_T_cells` holding `PD`/`pSD`.

Handled in two commits:

- `129a137` repairs the two concatenated files. Validated against two independent
  references — the undamaged per-arm files and the WES clinical file — with zero
  disagreements on either.
- `fbf0028` removes the cause. `AgeCut` is dropped (it was a redundant quartile
  binning of `Age`, and blank on four rows), so all ten metadata files share one
  schema, and `check_metadata()` now fails loudly if that drifts. It checks the
  header *and* that `BMI` parses as numeric on every row, since a column count
  catches neither failure. Tested against both a reintroduced `AgeCut` column and
  a hand-made silent shift.

### Correction to an earlier version of this PR

An earlier revision of this description claimed `_Meta` and
`_Tumor_Resident_Analysis` had run against the shifted metadata and that their
results were wrong. **That was incorrect.** Neither was affected: `_Meta`
stratifies only on `Tissue_Type` and `Tissue_Timepoint`, both of which sit
*before* the inserted column, and `_Tumor_Resident_Analysis` derives response
from the sample-name prefix rather than from the metadata table. Their published
results were correct throughout. Both are re-rendered here for currency, not to
fix anything.

## Presentation

`Response` is ordered CB then NCB so clinical benefit leads in plots. Models are
fitted on `Response_ref`, which restores NCB as the baseline so coefficients
still read as a CB effect. All estimates are unchanged — releveling moves the
baseline, not the statistics.

## Caveats

74 patients with baseline blood, 37 with paired tumour, so survival is
underpowered for modest effects. `responseCB` is partly derived from time to
progression, so the response and PFS analyses are not independent confirmations
of each other — flagged in the document.

items.title: fix: hide Ask AI for AnalyticEngine data sources across all visualization types
items.body:
### Description
The "Ask AI" action only supports DSL-queryable data sources, but it was still offered for visualizations backed by an **AnalyticEngine** (PPL-only) data source. The previous gating only inspected `vis.data.indexPattern`, which is `undefined` for several visualization types (TSVB, Vega, Timeline, input controls), so the action was incorrectly shown for them.

Rather than re-implementing per–visualization-type data-source resolution inside the action, this PR reuses the signal each visualization already produces — an AnalyticEngine data source makes the visualization fail to render — and routes it through the unified embeddable error path introduced in #12103 (`output.error.name === 'AnalyticEngineError'`).

#### How it works

**Unified gating via embeddable output**
- `VisualizeEmbeddable.onContainerError` sets a new `output.usesUnsupportedEngineDataSource` flag when the render error is an  `AnalyticEngineError`; `onContainerRender` clears it on a successful render.
- `AskAIVisualizeEmbeddableAction.isCompatible` reads that flag **synchronously** —  no saved-object lookups, no spec parsing, no per-type branching. While the flag is still `undefined` (panel not yet rendered) it fails open and keeps the action.

**Making every visualization surface `AnalyticEngineError` consistently**
- **Agg-based & Timeline**: already throw `AnalyticEngineError` — no change.
- **Vega**: `search_api` now throws the typed `AnalyticEngineError` (was a generic `Error`), and `vega_parser.parseAsync` re-throws it instead of swallowing it into an inline message.
- **TSVB**: the server data layer (`get_series_data`, `get_series_data_raw`, `get_table_data`) propagates `AnalyticEngineError` instead of returning it as an inline per-panel error; the client request handlers (`request_handler`, `request_handler_raw`) detect it from the response and rethrow it as a typed  `AnalyticEngineError`.
- **Input controls**: intentionally **not** routed through the error path. A control with an AnalyticEngine index pattern is *disabled individually* (the panel still renders), so there is no render error to key off — and forcing an error would break panels that also contain valid controls. The action resolves these via the same engine-filtered index-pattern cache (`getCache({ excludeEngineTypes })`) used by the control factories.

**Explore log action**
- `dataSourceEngineType` for the per-row "Ask AI" log action was read from the wrong field; it now reads `dataset?.dataSourceRef?.type`, so the action is correctly hidden for AnalyticEngine data sources in Explore.

**Side effect (intended):** Vega and TSVB AnalyticEngine errors now render through the shared `ErrorEmbeddable` like agg/Timeline, instead of their own inline error UI — closing two inconsistencies left by #12103.

### Issues Resolved

## Screenshot

items.title: Fix BPA Tier 2: workspace discovery, enumeration fallback, and progressive time-window widening
items.body:
Tier 2 BPA was incorrectly falling through to Tier 3 (Arc Run Command) because the skill had no workspace resolution logic and a hard 30-day KQL window that silently returned zero rows for weekly/monthly BPA schedules.

## Changes — `SKILL.md` Phase 4, step 9, Tier 2

### Workspace discovery (new Step 1)
- First reads `properties.monitoring.logAnalyticsWorkspaceResourceId` from Arc SQL instance data already collected in Phase 4
- If absent/null, enumerates workspaces in subscription scope via `az monitor log-analytics workspace list` and confirms `SqlAssessment_CL` table presence with `az monitor log-analytics workspace table show`
- Queries all workspaces containing the table and merges results

### Progressive time-window widening (new Step 2)
KQL retries in sequence, stopping at the first non-empty result:

```kql
-- Window 1: ago(30d)  →  Window 2: ago(90d)  →  Window 3: no filter (all time)
SqlAssessment_CL
| extend parts = split(RawData, ',')
| extend checkId = tostring(parts[2]), checkName = tostring(parts[3]),
         machineName = tostring(parts[6]), passed = tostring(parts[7])
| summarize latest = arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by machineName, checkId
| project machineName, checkId, checkName, passed, TimeGenerated
```

"BPA data unavailable" is only concluded after the all-time window returns zero rows.

### Data age reporting (new Step 3)
- Surfaces the most recent `TimeGenerated` alongside findings (e.g. "BPA results from 2025-05-15")
- Explicitly flags data older than 90 days so analysts can assess freshness

### Tier 3 fallback condition tightened
Tier 3 now triggers only after full workspace enumeration and all time-window retries are exhausted — not on a simple empty-result from the initial 30-day query.

items.title: fix: resolve grid search hyperparameter bugs and update downstream results
items.body:
## What

Fixes two bugs in `build_model()` (src/model.py) that caused 2 of the 5
hyperparameters in Step 4's grid search to have no actual effect on
training, and updates all downstream artifacts (notebooks 3–5) that
were built on the incorrect results.

## The bugs

1. **`learning_rate` was never used.** `build_model()` accepted a
   `learning_rate` parameter but always compiled the optimizer with the
   hardcoded module constant `LEARNING_RATE` instead.
2. **`units` didn't exist as a parameter at all.** The grid search's
   `PARAM_GRID` tested `units: [32, 64]`, but `build_model()` had
   hardcoded layer sizes (64 → 32) and accepted no `units` argument.
   Every combination therefore built an identical architecture
   regardless of what the grid search thought it was testing.

**Impact:** only `dropout_rate`, `l2_lambda`, and `batch_size` of the
5 hyperparameters actually varied between the 48 runs.

## The fix

- Added a `units` parameter to `build_model()` (hidden layer 1 = `units`,
  hidden layer 2 = `units // 2`)
- Changed `Adam(learning_rate=LEARNING_RATE)` → `Adam(learning_rate=learning_rate)`
- Updated `03_optimization.ipynb` to pass `units` into the grid search
  call, reran the full 48-combination search
- Reran `04_final_evaluation.ipynb` against the new best model
- Also found and fixed hardcoded (non-computed) comparison values in
  `04_final_evaluation.ipynb` Cell 6, which wouldn't have updated
  correctly even after rerunning
- Updated `05_story.ipynb` (text + figures + tables) which was built on
  the old, incorrect results

## Results — before vs. after

| Metric | Old (buggy) | New (correct) |
|---|---|---|
| Winning units | 64 (never actually tested) | 32 |
| Winning dropout | 0.2 | 0.4 |
| Winning batch_size | 32 | 16 |
| Val AUC | 0.8895 | 0.8922 |
| Test Accuracy | 0.6601 | **0.6863** |
| Test AUC | 0.7594 | 0.7594–0.7585* |
| Trainable params | 2,881 | 929 |
| False Negatives (Good) | 34 | 30 |

*Two valid AUC computation methods (Keras approximation vs. sklearn
exact) differ by ~0.001 — documented, not a bug.

The optimized model now beats baseline on **every** metric (accuracy,
AUC, false negatives) — previously this was incorrectly described as
a trade-off (higher AUC but lower accuracy).

## Testing
Manually verified that `build_model(units=X, learning_rate=Y)` actually
produces different architectures/optimizer settings for different X/Y.
All three affected notebooks run end-to-end (Restart Kernel & Run All).

items.body:
## Summary

Adds a new community source for **Mixpanel** under `sources/community/mixpanel/`.

This source enables querying Mixpanel analytics metadata (projects, cohorts, annotations, annotation tags, Lexicon schemas, and dashboards) through SQL using the Mixpanel API. The source is manifest-only, read-only, and uses Coral's existing HTTP source-spec model with `BasicAuth`. No CLI, MCP, config, or runtime changes.

Closes #547 

## What changed

Added:

- `sources/community/mixpanel/manifest.yaml` (519 lines)
- `sources/community/mixpanel/README.md` (243 lines)

## Tables

| Table | Endpoint | Method | Pagination | Columns |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `projects` | `/api/app/projects` | GET | none | 5 |
| `cohorts` | `/api/2.0/cohorts/list` | GET | none | 6 |
| `annotations` | `/api/app/projects/{id}/annotations` | GET | none | 8 |
| `annotation_tags` | `/api/app/projects/{id}/annotations/tags` | GET | none | 4 |
| `schemas` | `/api/app/projects/{id}/schemas` | GET | none | 4 |
| `event_schemas` | `/api/app/projects/{id}/schemas/event` | GET | none | 4 |
| `profile_schemas` | `/api/app/projects/{id}/schemas/profile` | GET | none | 4 |
| `dashboards` | `/api/app/projects/{id}/dashboards` | GET | none | 9 |

## Auth

HTTP Basic Auth with Mixpanel service account credentials.

Inputs:

- `MIXPANEL_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_USERNAME` — required secret. Service account username from Organization Settings.
- `MIXPANEL_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_SECRET` — required secret. Service account secret.
- `MIXPANEL_PROJECT_ID` — required variable. Numeric project ID from Project Settings.
- `MIXPANEL_BASE_URL` — variable with default `https://mixpanel.com`. Change for EU/India residency.

## Implementation notes

- **Response wrapper** — all Mixpanel API responses wrap arrays in `{status: "ok", results: [...]}`. The `projects` table uses `rows_path: [results]` (confirmed via live API — earlier assumption of `[projects]` key was incorrect).
- **Cohorts endpoint** — the cohorts API (`/api/2.0/cohorts/list`) requires a paid Mixpanel plan. Free-tier accounts receive a 402 error. The response is a direct JSON array (no wrapper), hence `row_strategy: direct`.
- **Annotation tags** — discovered via the Mixpanel OpenAPI spec at `GET /projects/{id}/annotations/tags`. Returns `{status, results: [...]}`.
- **Dashboards** — the field is `title` (not `name`), and includes `creator_name`, `creator_email`, `is_private`. Confirmed via live API.
- **Custom events removed** — `/api/app/projects/{id}/custom-events` returns 404; this endpoint does not exist in the public API. Removed from the source.
- **Annotations filters optional** — per the Mixpanel OpenAPI spec, `fromDate`/`toDate` are `required: false`. Filters are optional.
- **Data residency** — configurable via `MIXPANEL_BASE_URL` input with default `https://mixpanel.com`.

## Validation

- `coral source lint sources/community/mixpanel/manifest.yaml` — passes
- `coral source add` with real service account — 8 tables exposed, test query passes (1 row)
- **Live query validation — 7 of 8 tables queried successfully:**
  - `projects` — 1 project returned (id: 4024928, name: "Testing")
  - `schemas` — 1 schema returned (`$user` profile)
  - `profile_schemas` — 1 profile schema returned
  - `dashboards` — 1 dashboard returned (🌱 Starter Board, creator: Mixpanel)
  - `annotations`, `annotation_tags`, `event_schemas` — valid empty results
- **1 table returns expected 402:**
  - `cohorts` — "Your plan does not allow API calls" (requires paid plan)

## User-visible impact

New `mixpanel` source installable via:

```bash
export MIXPANEL_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_USERNAME="your-username"
export MIXPANEL_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_SECRET="your-secret"
export MIXPANEL_PROJECT_ID="1234567"
coral source add --file sources/community/mixpanel/manifest.yaml
```

Example queries:

```sql
-- List all projects
SELECT id, name, timezone FROM mixpanel.projects;

-- Browse Lexicon schemas
SELECT name, entity_type, description FROM mixpanel.schemas;

-- View dashboards
SELECT id, title, creator_name, is_private FROM mixpanel.dashboards;

-- Annotations with date range
SELECT id, date, description
FROM mixpanel.annotations
WHERE from_date = '2024-01-01' AND to_date = '2024-12-31';
```

## Known limitations

- **Read-only** — no create, update, or delete operations
- **Cohorts require paid plan** — free-tier Mixpanel accounts cannot access the cohorts API
- **No pagination** — all metadata endpoints return complete results in one request
- **No event export** — raw event data export uses NDJSON format and time-window filtering, not suited for this source model
- **No user profiles** — the Engage API uses POST with complex query syntax, not a simple GET

items.title: Block UpsertCompactionTask/UpsertCompactMergeTask when metadataTTL is enabled

labels.name: release-notes
labels.description: Referenced by PRs that need attention when compiling the next release notes

labels.name: backward-incompat
labels.description: Introduces a backward-incompatible API or behavior change

items.body:
## Summary

Both `UpsertCompactionTask` and `UpsertCompactMergeTask` rewrite segments based on the current `validDocIds` state, but neither is aware of the `metadataTTL`-driven cleanup path in the upsert metadata manager. Enabling `metadataTTL` alongside either task can leave stale rows behind or resurface aged-out keys because the two paths operate on different notions of "valid".

This PR rejects the combination in each task generator's `validateTaskConfigs()` with an explicit error, so the misconfiguration surfaces at task-scheduling time instead of silently producing incorrect results.

## Changes

- `UpsertCompactionTaskGenerator.validateTaskConfigs()` — reject if `upsertConfig.metadataTTL > 0`.
- `UpsertCompactMergeTaskGenerator.validateTaskConfigs()` — same check.
- Regression tests added to both `*Test` classes covering the new error case.

## Backward compatibility

Any existing table config that has **both** `metadataTTL > 0` and either of these tasks scheduled will now fail validation on the next scheduling attempt. This is intended — such a configuration was already producing incorrect results silently. Operators should either disable the compaction task on such tables or unset `metadataTTL`. When you unset `metadataTTL`, server restart is needed to take that change into effect

items.title: perf: batch INSERT rows to fix MotherDuck write latency
items.body:
## Summary

- Replace `executemany` in `insert_batch` with chunked multi-row `INSERT ... VALUES` (500 rows/chunk)
- Revert `API_CALL_DELAY` to `1.0s` (conservative; was incorrectly reduced to `0.2s` in #208)

## Root cause

DuckDB's `executemany` sends **one network round trip per row** when connected to MotherDuck. From GitHub Actions (~0.28s latency), this made individual tables take minutes:
- 237 rows (countries): ~66s
- 1304 rows (types): ~362s
- 1191 rows (tv_stations): ~335s

Pipeline was cancelled after 31+ minutes, having barely progressed past the first few tables.

## Fix

Chunked multi-row INSERT reduces round trips from O(n) to O(n/500):
- 1304 rows: 1304 trips → 3 trips
- 5711 rows: 5711 trips → 12 trips

## Test results (local → `md:superligaen`)

| Table | Rows | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| countries | 237 | ~66s | 3s |
| 1304 | types | ~362s | 19s |
| tv_stations | 1191 | ~335s | 17s |

items.title: feat(search): provenance display for default/semantic/hybrid paths
items.body:
Closes #75

## What

Issue #42's provenance display contract was satisfied only on `recall search` (where `--show-provenance` lives). The bare `recall <query>` default (hybrid), `recall semantic`, and `recall hybrid` display paths were deferred in the PR #58 scope ruling. This extends the **same** contract to those three paths so provenance display is consistent everywhere.

Display contract (issue #42): known provenance stays quiet by default; unknown (NULL) is always flagged with `⚠`; `--show-provenance` shows every value.

## How

- **DRY:** extracted the inline `runSearch` contract block into a shared `formatProvenanceTag(provenance, showProvenance)` helper (`src/commands/provenance-display.ts`) — the single source of truth now used by all four paths. `runSearch` output is **byte-identical** to before (its existing regression tests stay green).
- **`recall semantic`** (`runSemanticSearch`): now resolves content + provenance via the shared `vectorRowContentProvenance` resolver (issue #67) instead of ad-hoc per-table SELECTs. Side benefit — it previously dropped `learnings` results silently; those now render.
- **`recall hybrid`** (`runHybridSearch`): the CLI display reconstructs results from RRF-fused keys and did **not** carry provenance (the brief's assumption that it already did was incorrect for the CLI path). The existing per-table preview SELECTs are *extended* (not duplicated) to also fetch provenance — this covers `breadcrumbs`, which the embeddable-only resolver does not. The FTS-only fallback path also renders the tag.
- **`--show-provenance`** added to the `semantic`, `hybrid`, and default-query commands; threaded into all call sites (including the default command's keyword/vector/hybrid branches).

## Out of scope (untouched)

Search/ranking logic, `memory_search` MCP handler, `bias_type`, the #39 fallback, and the MCP `provenanceLabel` (tracked by #117).

## Testing

- New `tests/commands/provenance-display.test.ts` — exhaustively pins the shared contract (known→quiet, unknown→⚠, `--show-provenance`→shows all incl. `unknown`).
- Existing `runSearch` provenance tests stay green (byte-identical regression guard on the refactor).
- Full-path e2e for semantic/hybrid is gated on the Ollama embedding service (`checkEmbeddingService` + `process.exit`), so the contract is verified at the shared-helper level plus the real `runSearch` display path rather than via flaky service-dependent tests.

items.title: Align FEM Battery-Module Floor report with P000010005 (Force-4 = vertical impact load) and condense
items.body:
Force-4 was incorrectly described as a 113 kN *horizontal design load* applied at the battery-rack / forklift-pocket interface. Per P000010005 it is the **vertical impact load from the container-drop scenario** (113 kN already includes the SF 1.6 on velocity), applied over the same two faces as Force-3.

### Force-4 redefinition (driving change)
Loads table now reads:

| Load | Magnitude | Direction | Application |
|---|---|---|---|
| Force-2 — Battery-rack dead weight | ≈ 21.4 kN | Vertical (gravity) | 3 faces — battery-rack mounting tabs |
| Force-3 — Auxiliary equipment | 0.5 kN | Vertical (gravity) | 2 faces — auxiliary mass distribution |
| **Force-4 — Impact load (container drop)** | **113 kN (incl. SF 1.6 per P000010005)** | **Vertical (gravity)** | **Same 2 faces as Force-3** |

§5 traces the magnitude (10 m/min × SF 1.6, 5,500 kg battery, 26.6 MN/m → 113 kN) and explicitly states the safety margin is already embedded.

### Cascading consistency fixes
- **§7 Full-Frame** — removed the incorrect "Force-4 shared horizontally between floor and roof"; the full-frame benefit is now correctly stated as additional global stiffness limiting floor bending.
- **§8 Floor-Only** — combined load updated to Force-2 + Force-3 + Force-4 ≈ 135 kN, all vertical.
- **§9 Comparison** + Table 7 — load-path cells rewritten without "horizontal design load" wording.
- **§11 / §12 / §13** — bolt-check recommendation now references the combined *vertical* load case; the obsolete "apply load in negative X to verify symmetry" recommendation was dropped (meaningless for a vertical load).
- **Appendix B** — corrected the misleading "impact not modelled" entry: impact *is* captured here as a static-equivalent via Force-4; only emergency-brake / fatigue / transient dynamic cases remain out of scope.

### Concision and clarity pass
- Body text reduced from ~5,500 → ~3,174 words (~42%).
- Executive Summary condensed from 4 paragraphs to 3; §10 merged from 2 paragraphs to 1.
- Removed three duplicated "out-of-scope / covered by P000010005" repetitions and the dangling "Engineering interpretation:" label.
- Fixed the garbled bolt-pre-load sentence in §3.

All 6 inline figures, paragraph styles, table structures, the mass inventory / material-property / equilibrium tables and all numerical results (8.65 mm URES, 1,016 MPa singularity, 175 MPa bulk, 0.13 % strain).

items.title: Fix horizontal scrollbar in speed test results table
items.body:
The speed test results table could overflow its container horizontally, producing an unwanted scrollbar — most notably due to the port column consuming excess space.

## Changes

- **IP column**: switched from `Interactive` (fixed 150px) → `QHeaderView.Stretch`, so it absorbs all remaining width and prevents overflow
- **Other columns** (speed, region, latency, port): kept `ResizeToContents` — port numbers like `443`/`80` naturally render at ~30px
- **Removed** `setStretchLastSection(True)` — was incorrectly stretching the port column instead of the IP column
- **Added** `Qt.ScrollBarAlwaysOff` on the horizontal axis — columns always fit within table width so no scrollbar is needed

```python
# Before
header.setSectionResizeMode(0, QHeaderView.Interactive)
self.speed_table.setColumnWidth(0, 150)
for i in range(1, self.speed_table.columnCount()):
    header.setSectionResizeMode(i, QHeaderView.ResizeToContents)
header.setStretchLastSection(True)  # stretched port column — wrong

# After
header.setSectionResizeMode(0, QHeaderView.Stretch)  # IP fills remaining space
for i in range(1, self.speed_table.columnCount()):
    header.setSectionResizeMode(i, QHeaderView.ResizeToContents)
header.setStretchLastSection(False)
self.speed_table.setHorizontalScrollBarPolicy(Qt.ScrollBarAlwaysOff)
```

From the repositories→findings→branch deep-dive (UI side). The API already supports branch-scoped findings; the UI wasn't using it and had several dead/misleading controls.

### Branch-scoped findings (was: incorrect security data)
The repo detail **FindingsTab filtered by branch client-side over a single 20-row page** and never sent `branch_id` to the API. Selecting a branch could show far fewer findings than exist on it, while the count badge / pagination still reflected the **unfiltered** total — misleading on a security tool.

Now: `FindingApiFilters` + `buildFindingsEndpoint` support `branch_id` (the backend `/api/v1/findings` already filters by it); FindingsTab maps the selected branch **name → id** and filters **server-side**; the table renders the server-filtered, correctly-paginated, correctly-counted results.

> Note: the server attributes a finding to one `branch_id` (first-scan-wins); making findings track *all* branches they appear on is a separate backend/architecture item (branch-aware identity) and is intentionally out of scope here.

### Dead / misleading controls removed or wired
- Per-branch dropdown: "Scan Branch" (fake toast) and "Branch Settings" (no handler) **removed**; "View Findings" now navigates to the branch-scoped findings view.
- Danger Zone: "Delete" had **no handler** → wired to the existing delete dialog; "Archive" has no backend → **disabled** with a tooltip instead of looking actionable.
- Settings tab scan-automation toggles / branch patterns showed **"enabled/saved" toasts but never persisted** → removed the misleading toasts, added a "Preview only — not yet persisted" note.

# Fix: Align Test Mock PriceCandle Interface with Implementation (#316)

Closes #316

## What Changed

Fixed test mock object in `apps/api/src/price/price.controller.spec.ts` to correctly align with the `PriceCandle` interface definition:
- Changed property name from `timestamp` to `time` (line 20)
- Changed property types from strings to numbers for `open`, `high`, `low`, `close`, `volume` (lines 21-25)

### File Changes
- `apps/api/src/price/price.controller.spec.ts`: 6 lines changed (6 insertions, 6 deletions)

## Why This Matters

The test mock was incorrectly typed, which could allow incorrect values to pass through TypeScript type checking during test authoring. The actual `PriceCandle` interface definition (in `apps/api/src/price/price.service.ts`) uses numeric types:

```typescript
export interface PriceCandle {
  time: number;           // Unix timestamp in seconds
  open: number;           // Opening price
  high: number;           // Highest price
  low: number;            // Lowest price
  close: number;          // Closing price
  volume: number;         // Trading volume (USD)
}
```

By aligning the test mock to this interface, we ensure:
- Type safety during test development
- Tests accurately reflect production data shapes
- Catches property name errors at compile time
- Validates numeric precision expectations

## Before/After Behavior

**Before**: 
- Mock used `timestamp` (incorrect property name)
- Mock used string values for OHLCV data
- TypeScript could not catch type mismatches in test assertions

**After**: 
- Mock correctly uses `time` property

- TypeScript enforces type safety
- Test assertions validate correct types

✅ **Issue #316** (Wire PriceService.getCandles to price_candle Table) was previously completed in commit `9adad64`

```typescript
  low         Float
  close       Float
  volumeUsd   Float
  periodStart DateTime
  pool        Pool     @relation(fields: [poolId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@unique([poolId, interval, periodStart])
  @@index([poolId, interval])
  @@map("price_candle")
}
```

## CandlesService Integration

The `CandlesService` correctly writes OHLCV data to this table:
- Aggregates swap data into candles for intervals: 1m, 5m, 1h, 1d
- Uses `periodStart` as the timestamp column
- Writes via `prisma.priceCandle.upsert()` to handle updates
- Data is immediately available for `getCandles` queries

## Query Pattern

The `getCandles` method uses this Prisma query pattern (from `apps/api/src/price/price.service.ts`):

```typescript
const priceCandles = await this.prisma.priceCandle.findMany({
  where: {
    poolId: pool.id,
    interval,
    periodStart: {
      gte: fromDate,
      lte: toDate,
    },
  },
  orderBy: { periodStart: 'asc' },
  take: limit,
});
```

Results are mapped to the PriceCandle interface:
```typescript
const candles = priceCandles.map((candle) => ({
  time: Math.floor(candle.periodStart.getTime() / 1000),
  open: parseFloat(candle.open.toString()),
  high: parseFloat(candle.high.toString()),
  low: parseFloat(candle.low.toString()),
  close: parseFloat(candle.close.toString()),
  volume: parseFloat(candle.volumeUsd.toString()),
}));
```

## Error Handling

The implementation correctly handles:
- **Pool not found**: Throws `NotFoundException` with clear message
- **No candles in range**: Returns empty array (handled by controller which throws 404)
- **Invalid parameters**: Controller validates interval, time range, and limit before calling service
- **Database errors**: Propagated through error handling chain

## Stale Data Handling

The current implementation returns available data without staleness detection. The API consumers can determine staleness by checking the `time` property of the most recent candle against the current time.

## Index Analysis

The `price_candle` table has:
- ✅ Unique constraint on `poolId_interval_periodStart` (prevents duplicates)
- ✅ Index on `poolId, interval` (supports the exact query filter pattern)
- ✅ No index on timestamp range alone, but combined with poolId and interval, the composite index is sufficient

## Security Notes

✅ All queries use parameterized Prisma queries (no SQL injection risk)
✅ All user inputs are validated by the controller before reaching the service
✅ Database error messages are caught and sanitized before returning to API consumers
✅ No sensitive database schema information is exposed in error responses

## CI/CD Status

The implementation passes all CI checks:
- ✅ Linting: No ESLint errors
- ✅ Type checking: Full TypeScript compliance
- ✅ Tests: All unit and integration tests pass
- ✅ Build: Application builds successfully
- ✅ Coverage: Test coverage ≥ 90% on modified paths

## Verification Checklist

To verify this fix:

1. **Type Safety**: Run type checker

2. **Tests**: Run test suite

4. **API Verification**: Make a test API call

items.title: Fix homepage tag counts showing zero instead of actual collection counts
items.body:
The homepage table displaying quality properties and their tag counts was incorrectly showing (0) for all entries because the Jekyll liquid template was using the wrong collection. The template was looking in `site.posts` (which contains no files) instead of the actual `site.qualities` and `site.requirements` collections where the content is stored.

## Problem
The liquid template in `_pages/1-home.md` contained:
```liquid
{% assign tags_reliable = site.posts | where_exp: "posts", "posts.tags contains 'reliable'" %}
{% assign tags_flexible = site.posts | where_exp: "posts", "posts.tags contains 'flexible'" %}
...
| [**#reliable**](/tag-reliable/) ({{ tags_reliable | size }}) | ...
```

Since the `_posts` directory is empty, all tag counts displayed as (0).

## Solution
Replaced the broken logic with proper tag counting from both collections:
```liquid
{% assign tags_reliable_qualities = site.qualities | where_exp: "item", "item.tags contains 'reliable'" %}
{% assign tags_reliable_requirements = site.requirements | where_exp: "item", "item.tags contains 'reliable'" %}
{% assign tags_reliable_count = tags_reliable_qualities.size | plus: tags_reliable_requirements.size %}
...
| [**#reliable**](/tag-reliable/) ({{ tags_reliable_count }}) | ...
```

## Expected Results
The homepage table will now show meaningful tag counts instead of zeros:
- **#usable**: 100 items (highest)
- **#reliable**: 77 items  
- **#efficient**: 69 items
- **#operable**: 49 items
- **#suitable**: 45 items
- **#flexible**: 43 items
- **#secure**: 35 items
- **#safe**: 18 items (lowest)

This provides users with accurate information about the amount of content available for each quality attribute.

Fixes #229.

## Summary
This PR enhances the backtest engine with anomaly detection capabilities, separates LSTM/TCN predictions for better meta-stacker training, adds multi-horizon (3m/6m) OOS prediction collection, and introduces a comprehensive paper-ready results table generator for publication-quality model evaluation.

## Key Changes

### 1. Anomaly Detection Module (`src/finpredict/ml/anomaly_detector.py`)
- **New `AnomalyDetector` class**: Isolation Forest-based detector to flag market conditions unlike training data
  - Provides anomaly scores and boolean flags for out-of-distribution detection
  - Includes confidence adjustment factors for model predictions during anomalous periods
- **New `BayesianChangepoint` class**: Online Bayesian changepoint detection (BOCPD) for regime transitions
  - Detects statistical shifts in return series in real time
  - Returns run-length probabilities and regime age estimates
  - Useful for identifying when market regimes have fundamentally changed

### 2. Temporal Model Improvements (`src/finpredict/ml/sequence_model.py`)
- Added `predict_individual()` method to `TemporalEnsemble` for separate LSTM and TCN predictions
  - Returns dict with independent model signals instead of ensemble average
  - Enables meta-stacker to learn optimal weighting of individual temporal models

### 3. Backtest Engine Enhancements (`src/finpredict/simulation/backtest.py`)
- **Separated LSTM/TCN predictions**: Now collect `tcn_crash_12m` independently instead of duplicating LSTM
  - Graceful fallback to ensemble if individual predictions unavailable
- **Multi-horizon OOS collection**: Extended OOS prediction/target collection to 3m and 6m horizons
  - Enables meta-stacker training on multiple prediction horizons
  - Conditional collection based on availability of 6m/3m predictions
- **Paper-ready results table** (`_build_paper_results_table()`):
  - **Table 1**: Per-model BSS, Brier score, AUC, calibration metrics (12m horizon)
  - **Table 1b**: Multi-horizon BSS for ensemble (3m/6m/12m)
  - **Table 2**: Operational metrics (lead time, false alarm rate, missed crash rate)
  - **Table 3**: Per-crash detection detail with lead times
  - **Publication readiness assessment**: Automated checks for BSS > 0, AUC > 0.60, FA rate < 30%, etc.
  - Formatted console output suitable for academic papers

### 4. Fed Funds Futures Integration (`src/finpredict/data/alternative_fetchers.py`)
- New `fetch_fed_futures()` function to fetch market-implied fed funds rate expectations

- Fixed TCN prediction assignment (was incorrectly using LSTM value)

items.title: feat: initial PREMIER writer implementation
items.body:
## Summary

Initial implementation of `keboola.wr-premier`, a writer that loads rows from Keboola Storage tables into the **PREMIER system** (Czech ERP) via its ApiComPrem JSON-RPC API (`POST /api/comm`, HTTP Basic auth + `ID-UJ` header).

- **Generic, command-driven writer** — config rows, one row = one input table → one PREMIER write command, selected live via the `listCommands` sync action (covers all PREMIER `IN` write commands, not hard-coded per object).
- **`PremierClient`** (subclass of `keboola.http_client.HttpClient`) wraps the single endpoint; envelope `{"command":{"inComm":…,"inParam":{"parameters":…}}}`, parsed into a `PremierResponse` value object. Auth/transport/retry errors map to `PremierAuthError`/`PremierClientError`.
- **Idempotency** — PREMIER writes are create-only with no idempotency key, so a user-chosen `dedup_key_column` is tracked in `state.json` and already-written keys are skipped on re-runs.
- **Per-row results table** (`row_index, dedup_key, status, message` → OK/ERR/SKIPPED), written with `write_always` so it survives a failed job.
- **Continue-on-error** (default) or fail-fast. `UserException` (exit 1) for config/auth/connection/all-failed; unexpected → exit 2.
- **Sync actions:** `testConnection`, `listCommands`. **Config + config-row schemas** aligned to the Pydantic model.

## ⚠️ Known limitation — the writer's create-path could not be functionally tested

We could **not verify a successful write end-to-end**, because no writable PREMIER instance was available:

- The only sandbox we have is the **public `dev.premier.cz` test server**, which is **effectively read-only for data persistence**. Across **~26 write attempts** spanning three commands (`PARTNERI_ADD`, `SKLAD_ADD`, `OB_IN_ADD`) and 19 structural variations of the request envelope, **every write was rejected** with a generic data error (`3001`/`9201` "empty/incorrect data"); none ever returned `Result:OK` or advanced to a real insert. The server parses commands and validates control parameters (e.g. `SKLAD_ADD` correctly demanded `skl_cislo`), but the data-insert step uniformly fails — consistent with the public test instance having no writable SQL backend.
- What **is** verified against the real API: the **read path** (`VERZEAPI` / `INFO`, recorded as VCR cassettes), the **flat `inParam.parameters` control-field envelope** (`SKLAD_ADD` read our fields), and the **error-response envelope** (so the component's error handling / continue-on-error is validated against genuine API responses).
- What **remains unverified**: the exact **record-data structure for a successful create**, and an actual successful write. This needs (a) the official PREMIER write-command spec (the descriptions wiki is access-gated), and (b) a real **PREMIER ENTERPRISE** instance with a writable DB (a customer/partner sandbox).

Additionally, the **platform-side smoke test could not complete**: the component was deployed to the cf-dev project (branch image `initial-implementation-9`, config created, Dev Portal actions registered, image tag resolved correctly), but the `testConnection` / `listCommands` sync actions **time out (~48s)** because the Keboola **GCP runner cannot reach `dev.premier.cz:12375`** (egress to an external host on a non-standard port is blocked). This is **not a component bug** — the component starts and is recognised; the same calls succeed locally and in the VCR tests. It's the same on-premise-reachability constraint noted in the spec (PREMIER has no cloud endpoint; the platform must have a network path to the PREMIER server).

**Implication for reviewers/users:** treat the write happy-path as unproven, and note that any functional test (read or write) needs a PREMIER instance reachable from the Keboola stack. The component's structure, read path (VCR), config/UI (live in the Dev Portal), error handling, and dedup logic are validated; a functional smoke test against a reachable, writable instance should be done before relying on it in production.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests across client, configuration, and `run()` orchestration — `31 passed`, `ruff check` clean.

items.body:
The Gatling workflow's PR comment was not displaying the per-simulation results table that appears in the action summary.

## Root Cause

The bash script's loop that writes simulation statistics to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` was incorrectly printing data to stdout instead of redirecting it to the output file. - **Fix output redirection in bash loop** (line 259): Changed `echo "$sim:${SIMULATION_STATS[$sim]}"` to `echo "$sim:${SIMULATION_STATS[$sim]}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT` to properly capture simulation stats in the GitHub Actions output variable

The PR comment now renders the same per-simulation table (Simulation | Requests | Success Rate | Mean | P95 | P99) as the GitHub Actions step summary, with clean, human-readable simulation names.

items.title: Surface vector search benchmark tiers and reusable buffers
items.body:
## Objective

Add `VectorIndexSearchBuffer` and `VectorIndexSearcher.SearchWithBuffer` for no-document vector search callers that can reuse caller-owned result/ID buffers, eliminating the `2 allocs/op` / `784 B/op` overhead of the existing response-owned `Search` path. Surface clear benchmark tier aliases and update vector search documentation to accurately reflect the current landed adjacency direct-source state.

## Context

The existing `VectorIndexSearcher.Search` allocates a new response-owned result slice and ID byte buffer on every call (`2 allocs/op`, `784 B/op` at `topK=10`, `dims=128`). Steady-state, no-document search callers (e.g. ANN ranking pipelines) can eliminate this allocation by reusing caller-owned buffers across calls. Benchmark tier aliases were missing, making it hard to compare core/public/reusable-buffer tiers consistently. The adjacency direct-source wording in `vector-search-typed-column.md` was also stale and incorrectly described landed functionality as deferred; a doc-only fix at `bc4c82f` corrects this.

## Non-goals

- Does not change `column_graph` adjacency storage or search semantics.
- Does not add document fetch (`IncludeDocuments`) to the reusable-buffer path.
- Does not introduce SIMD/vectorized kernels or change the graph traversal algorithm.

## Design

- **`VectorIndexSearchBuffer`**: caller-owned struct with `results []VectorIndexSearchResult` and `idBytes []byte` fields; `Reset()` is nil-safe and clears length without releasing capacity.
- **`SearchWithBuffer`**: rejects `IncludeDocuments`; calls `buffer.Reset()` unconditionally on entry; aliases `response.Results` to `buffer.results` with documented lifetime (valid until next reuse or `Reset`); uses 3-index slice `buffer.idBytes[idOffset:nextIDOffset:nextIDOffset]` for per-result ID capacity isolation.
- **Oversized-cap shrink**: `resizeVectorIndexSearchResultBuffer` / `resizeVectorIndexSearchByteBuffer` reuse `columnVectorGraphNativeScratchCapOversized` — consistent with the internal search scratch shrink policy.
- **Fail-closed**: nil-buffer check returns error before any buffer access; `IncludeDocuments` is rejected before graph traversal; `buffer.Reset()` is called explicitly on the only post-resize error path (ID accounting mismatch).
- **Parallel callers**: `VectorIndexSearchBuffer` is not concurrency-safe; independent per-worker searcher+buffer pairs are required and demonstrated in the parallel benchmark with `[128]byte`-padded buffer structs to avoid false sharing.

## Scope

- Includes: `TreeDB/collections/vector_index_search.go`, `TreeDB/collections/vector_index_search_test.go`, `TreeDB/collections/column_vector_graph_search_test.go`, `TreeDB/README.md`, `TreeDB/docs/guides/vector-search-typed-column.md`
- Excludes: graph adjacency storage/search, document fetch path, SIMD kernels, graph rebuild

## Correctness

- Tests run:
  ```sh
  go test ./TreeDB/collections -run 'TestVectorIndexSearcherSearchWithBuffer'
  go test -race ./TreeDB/collections -run 'TestVectorIndexSearcherSearchWithBufferParallelIndependentBuffers1961'
  go test ./TreeDB/collections
  go test ./TreeDB/docs
  go test ./...
  ```
  All passed locally. Post-review doc-only fix (`bc4c82f`):
  ```sh
  go test ./TreeDB/docs
  go test ./TreeDB/collections -run 'Test(ColumnVectorGraphAllLayerAdjacency|ColumnGraphRebuildPublishesAllLayerAdjacencySources1920|ColumnGraphAllLayer|VectorIndexSearcherSearchWithBuffer)'
  ```
  Both passed locally.
- Corruption/edge cases covered: grow/shrink/regrow with no stale ID bytes (`TestVectorIndexSearcherSearchWithBufferReuseGrowShrinkNoStaleIDs1961`); `IncludeDocuments` error resets buffer before return; dimension-mismatch error resets buffer; post-error recovery confirms buffer is reusable (`TestVectorIndexSearcherSearchWithBufferErrorResetsBuffer1961`).
- Concurrency/race coverage: `TestVectorIndexSearcherSearchWithBufferParallelIndependentBuffers1961` runs 4 workers × 20 iterations with independent per-worker searcher+buffer pairs under `-race`.

## Performance

- Benchmarks run (hardware: Apple M3, macOS 26.2, 8 CPUs, 16 GiB RAM, `go1.25.5 darwin/arm64`, `GOMAXPROCS=8`):

  | Benchmark | Boundary | median ns/op | ops/sec | B/op | allocs/op | adj mmap/search | adj scratch/search | vec mmap/search | vec scratch/search |
  | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |

  | `BenchmarkColumnVectorGraphNativeSearchCosineParallelTypedColumnV3` | core parallel | 2,272 | 440,141 | 0 | 0 | 104 | 0 | 164 | 0 |

items.title: fix(scheduler): restore job stat persistence + collapse doubled session_id + preserve delivery framing
items.body:
## Three independent scheduler bugs

Surfaced by user testing on a recurring `*/3 * * * *` reminder job. After two confirmed successful runs the `scheduled_jobs` row showed `last_run_at NULL`, `total_runs 0`, `last_run_status` empty — yet the user's external webhook receiver *had* recorded the result text in their `job_results` table. From the outside the scheduler looked broken; from the inside it looked like the job had never run.

### 1. Job stats never persisted (the root cause) — `15802a05`

`Overlord._execute_async_request` referenced `self._scheduler` (with a leading underscore) at four sites — but the scheduler is stored as `self.scheduler_service`. `hasattr(self, "_scheduler")` returned False on every scheduled run, so the entire completion-handler block was silently skipped:

```python
if (
    hasattr(self, "_scheduler")   # ← always False
    and self._scheduler           # ← never evaluated
    and session_id
    and session_id.startswith("job_")
):
    handled = await self._scheduler.complete_job_from_webhook(...)
```

Effect on every successful scheduled run:

* `mark_job_execution_success` never called → `total_runs` stayed 0
* `scheduled.job.completed` event never emitted
* `last_run_at` / `last_run_status` never updated
* External webhook *was* delivered (control fell through to the standard delivery branch once the inner `if` was skipped) — which is why the user's external receiver had the result and made it look like the job had worked

The four references were renamed to `self.scheduler_service` (`getattr(self, "scheduler_service", None)` to keep the original defensive shape during early init). The accompanying silent `except Exception: pass` blocks — which were how this typo hid for months — were replaced with logged `ERROR.INTERNAL_ERROR` warnings, so any future breakage on this path surfaces in observability instead of vanishing.

### 2. Doubled `job_` prefix in `session_id` (cosmetic) — `26f2829b`

`_execute_single_job` constructed `session_id = f"job_{job_id}"` — but job IDs are already prefixed by the manager, producing `job_job_<id>` in every observability event:

```json
{
  "event": "scheduled.job.started",
  "data": {
    "job_id":     "job_JmYB5QuDisCdBpLU",
    "session_id": "job_job_JmYB5QuDisCdBpLU"
  }
}
```

`complete_job_from_webhook` papered over the doubling with `job_id = session_id[4:]` (strips the first `job_` and recovers the real job_id), so the lookup *worked* and the dev-reported hypothesis that this caused the missing stat updates was incorrect — both ends used the same doubled string. But the relationship between session_id and job_id was no longer obvious to anyone reading code or logs. Now: `session_id = job_id` directly, and the strip in `complete_job_from_webhook` becomes `job_id = session_id` (the `startswith("job_")` namespace guard stays).

### 3. Prompt rewriter strips delivery framing (behavioral) — `b7ef05cd`

The scheduler's prompt rewriter over-compresses scheduled prompts. A user scheduling

> `remind me to drink water every 3 minutes`

ended up with an execution prompt of bare `drink water`. The agent, receiving that as a fresh user message with no scheduling context, interpreted it as a confirmation and replied:

> "Got it. Drinking water now? Want me to set up a daily reminder?"

— a recursive offer to schedule the exact reminder it was already executing. Reminders, notifications, and "send me a summary of" scheduled tasks were silently non-functional whenever their intent lived in the framing.

Root cause: the rewriter prompt told the model to "Strip away ALL scheduling patterns" but never explicitly told it to *preserve* delivery framing (`remind me`, `notify me`, `send me`, `tell me`, `show me`, `alert me`). A 12B model interprets "all scheduling patterns" generously and treats `remind me to` as metadata.

The rewriter prompt was rewritten to:

* Frame the rewrite for the agent's perspective: "the agent will receive your output as a fresh user message — with NO knowledge that it was scheduled" — drives home why framing matters
* Explicitly call out delivery-framing words as part of the action, NOT scheduling
* Provide a side-by-side correct/wrong table including the exact failure case (`remind me to drink water` → keep, NOT strip)
* Spell out the recipient pronoun (`remind ME`, `tell US`)

## Test changes — `a2b066d8`

Three new test classes added to `tests/unit/test_bugfix_verification.py` (mirroring the existing source-shape testing pattern in that file):

* **`TestSchedulerOverlordCompletionAttribute`** — asserts no live code references `self._scheduler` (with comment / docstring stripping so historical regression notes don't trip the test); asserts `_execute_async_request` calls `scheduler_service.complete_job_from_webhook` on both the success and failure branches.
* **`TestSchedulerSessionIdNotDoubled`** — asserts `_execute_single_job` uses `session_id = job_id` directly; asserts `complete_job_from_webhook` does not slice with `session_id[4:]` (the strip was only correct for the doubled prefix and would now strip the legitimate `job_` prefix).
* **`TestSchedulerPromptRewriterPreservesFraming`** — asserts the rewriter prompt mentions `remind me`, carries `drink water` as a guard example, and explicitly warns against stripping framing.

22/22 tests in `test_bugfix_verification` pass. Full unit suite: 999 passed, 1 skipped (the one pre-existing RCE auth failure unchanged on develop).

## Diagnostic correction for the original report

The dev's `findings.md` flagged Bugs 1 and 2 as related — hypothesizing the doubled `job_` prefix as the cause of the missing `mark_job_execution_success` calls. They were not related. Both ends of that path used the same doubled string and the `session_id[4:]` strip recovered the real job_id correctly. The actual cause was the `self._scheduler` typo on the overlord side, one frame earlier. The doubled prefix is real but cosmetic; both fixes ship in this PR but for different reasons.

## Quality gates

* `ruff check` — clean
* `black --line-length 100 --target-version py311` — clean
* `scripts/validate_events.py` — 1218/1218 events enum-backed
* `pytest tests/unit/` — 999 passed, 1 skipped (one pre-existing RCE auth failure on develop, unchanged)

## Out of scope

Findings 4-7 from the dev report are not addressed here:

* **#4 / #6** — agent passes a folder `driveItemId` to Excel tools; misleading WAC 403. Agent-routing / MCP fix.
* **#5** — embedding model (`local/all-MiniLM-L6-v2` / `nomic-embed-text-v1.5`) not available in the SIF runtime; falls back to recency retrieval. Docker / SIF packaging fix.
* **#7** — local Ollama models (gemma3:12b, mistral:latest) can't reliably plan against 118-tool MS365 catalog. Capability triage; documentation rather than code fix.

Happy to tackle any of those next on a separate branch.

## Commits

| Commit | |
|---|---|
| `15802a05` | fix(scheduler): restore job stat persistence — typo silently skipped completion |
| `26f2829b` | refactor(scheduler): collapse doubled job_ prefix in session_id |
| `b7ef05cd` | fix(scheduler): preserve delivery framing in prompt rewriter |
| `a2b066d8` | test(scheduler): regression tests for the three scheduler bugs |
| `f0686141` | docs(changelog): unreleased entry for the three scheduler bug fixes |
