items.title: NPT-1068: Fix Modeled BMP Performance panel on Treatment BMP detail
items.body:
## Summary

Multiple related SPA-migration regressions on the Treatment BMP detail page (and one on the WQMP detail page), all surfaced while testing BMP ID 35 (Constructed Wetland, ALV-CW-DFW-1) which was rendering a completely blank Modeled BMP Performance panel.

### 1. Modeling Attributes / Modeled BMP Performance shared one gate
Both cards were wrapped in `@if (hasModelingAttributes)`, so BMP types analyzed in modeling but without custom Modeling-purpose attributes silently hid both panels. Legacy MVC had two distinct gates: `HasModelingAttributes` (attribute editor) and `IsAnalyzedInModelingModule` (performance panel).

- Added `IsAnalyzedInModelingModule` (denormalized from `TreatmentBMPType`) to `TreatmentBMPDto` + projection.
- Sourced it on the SPA component instead of the unassigned-`true` placeholder.
- Split the `@if` so each card has its own gate.

### 2. `IsFullyParameterized` was always null on the DTO
The computation joins BMP + type's modeling config + the `vTreatmentBMPModelingAttributes` view + delineation verification, so it can't be expressed as an EF projection — and the projection didn't try. The DTO always serialized `null`, so `@if (!treatmentBMP.IsFullyParameterized)` always fired and rendered the "missing fields required" fallback even for fully-parameterized BMPs.

- Compute it post-materialize in `GetByIDAsDtoAsync`, same shape as the existing `OtherTreatmentBMPsExistInSubbasin` / `HasSettableBenchmarkAndThresholdValues` supplemental loads.
- `TreatmentBMPModelingType` is a static lookup class (resolved via `AllLookupDictionary` at runtime), not an EF navigation, so no `ThenInclude`.
- Use the **upstreamest BMP's** delineation, not this BMP's own — downstream BMPs inherit their upstream's verified delineation. Mirrors the pattern in `vTreatmentBMPUpstreams.ListWithDelineationAsDictionary`. (Caught by Copilot on initial pass.)

### 3. `<modeled-bmp-performance>` received `[loadReducingResult]="null"`
Per-BMP modeled performance was never migrated. Legacy MVC had `TreatmentBMPController.GetModelResults` returning an MVC-only DTO. The SPA component existed but the parent component hardcoded `null`, so all the tables showed blank cells once we got the gating right.

- New `TreatmentBMPModeledPerformance.GetByBMPIDAsync` mirrors the Detailed-approach branch of `WaterQualityManagementPlanModeledPerformance.GetModeledPerformanceAsync`, keyed on `TreatmentBMPID` against `vLoadReducingResults` (non-baseline).
- New `GET /treatment-bmps/{id}/load-reducing-result` endpoint returning `ProjectLoadReducingResultDto`. **Returns 200 with a null body** when Nereid hasn't produced a result yet (avoids devtools 404 noise on the common case).
- SPA template falls back to a "results not yet available" message when the async pipe sees null.

### 4. Restored Modeled BMP Performance footer (NPT-1068 follow-up)
Legacy MVC's `ModeledPerformance.cshtml` had three footer rows under the table that the SPA migration dropped:

- "Results last calculated at MM/dd/yyyy h:mm a" — driven from `LastCalculatedDate`.
- "Latest Nereid Request | Latest Nereid Response" — Sitka-admin only, gated to the same condition as the legacy view. New `TreatmentBMPNereidLogContentDto` + `NereidLogs.GetLatestForTreatmentBMPAsDtoAsync` + `GET /treatment-bmps/{id}/latest-nereid-log` (`[SitkaAdminFeature]`). SPA fetches lazily on click and triggers a blob download matching the legacy MVC's client-side download pattern. Endpoint **returns 200+null body** when no log exists; SPA pushes a warning alert if a click resolves null. Real failures (auth/network/5xx) push a danger alert via the subscribe error callback.
- "About Modeling BMP Performance" — points at the legacy MVC `/Home/AboutModelingBMPPerformance` URL for now. NPT-1068-1 stands up the SPA `/modeling-calculations` equivalent and will repoint this when it lands.

### 5. WQMP detail: "Learn about WQMP Modeling Options" link
Legacy MVC WQMP detail had a help link next to the Modeling Approach heading in the BMPs card; the SPA migration dropped it. Restored with the same right-aligned placement. Points at the legacy MVC `/WaterQualityManagementPlan/WqmpModelingOptions` URL for now; NPT-1068-1 will repoint to `/wqmp-modeling-options`. Lifted the actions cluster out of the `<h4>` heading so the link doesn't inherit h4 styling.

## Net effect

BMP 35 (and any other modeled BMP) now renders the populated Total / Dry / Wet performance tables plus the legacy footer rows. Non-modeled BMP types (trash screens, etc.) correctly hide the panel. Modeled BMPs that haven't been processed by Nereid show the "results not yet available" message. Downstream BMPs that inherit an upstream delineation are now correctly recognized as fully parameterized. WQMP detail surfaces the modeling-options help link.

## Test plan

- [x] `dotnet build Neptune.sln` clean; `cd Neptune.Web && npm run build-dev` clean.
- [ ] BMP 35 (ALV-CW-DFW-1, Constructed Wetland): Modeled BMP Performance panel renders with populated numbers across Total / Dry / Wet tabs.
- [ ] A trash-only BMP (e.g. Inlet And Trash Screen): Modeling Attributes + Modeled BMP Performance panels both hidden.
- [ ] A BMP that is analyzed in modeling but has no custom modeling attributes for its type: Modeling Attributes panel hidden; Modeled BMP Performance panel still renders.
- [ ] A modeled BMP that hasn't been parameterized: Modeled BMP Performance panel renders the "missing fields required" message.
- [ ] A downstream BMP that inherits an upstream verified delineation: now shows the performance numbers (was incorrectly showing "missing fields" pre-Copilot fix).
- [ ] As a Sitka admin: "Latest Nereid Request | Latest Nereid Response" links appear and download the JSON. Non-Sitka admin users don't see them.
- [ ] WQMP detail page: "Learn about WQMP Modeling Options" link visible next to the Modeling Approach heading; Edit button (editors only) aligned with other panel Edit buttons.

## v0.2.1 (2026-07-17)

Open-source release. Closes the gap between the Resolver Pipeline and the query/verify surfaces (call-graph `resolve_strategy` propagation, module-tree JSON validity, capability verifier LIKE-direction, module-hierarchy materialisation), plus FFI boundary detection, paginated graph export, LadybugDB embedded storage, one-click bootstrap, and a full code-review / portability / documentation pass.

### 🚀 New Features

- **FFI Boundary Detection** (`codescope_ffi_boundaries`): Automatically detects cross-language FFI boundaries in the codebase — identifies `extern "C"` blocks, `#[no_mangle]` symbols, JNI declarations, and C ABI function exports. Helps developers audit unsafe interop surface.
- **Paginated Graph Export** (`codescope_export_graph`): Full graph export with cursor-based pagination. Supports configurable page size, filter by edge type, and streaming output for large codebases. Integrates with MCP tooling for seamless client-side consumption.
- **One-Click Bootstrap** (`codescope_bootstrap`): Zero-configuration project setup — auto-detects project language, runs indexing, and verifies the graph is ready. Single command from clone to queryable graph.
- **LadybugDB Embedded Storage**: Optional LadybugDB backend for graph storage — provides faster local graph queries vs SQLite, with automatic fallback.
- **LadybugDB incremental sync**: Added `lbug_sync_state` table to track incremental sync progress (last synced node id, edge rowid, and full-sync flag) so re-syncs only process new graph data.
- **ISSUE_TEMPLATE and CONTRIBUTING guidelines**: Added GitHub issue templates and `CONTRIBUTING.md` to guide open-source contributors.

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- **`resolve_strategy` not propagated to `graph_edges`**: Visitor-level `resolve_strategy` (`p1_intra` / `external` / `unresolved`) was correctly written to `semantic_records` but never reached `graph_edges` through the Resolver Pipeline. `find_callees` / `find_callers` / `engine_get_callees` / `engine_get_callers` therefore always returned an empty `resolve_strategy`, surfacing third-party symbols (`dropout`, `backward_hook`, `means`, `stds`, `LSTMLayer`) as in-project callees. Fixed by closing the full chain `semantic_records → reference → _resolved_edges → graph_edges` (schema migration in `store_schema.cpp`, staging in `pipeline.cpp`, output restored in `query_engine.cpp` + `store_query.cpp`). Verified on `bun` (8 languages): 100% of `edge_type=1` (call) edges carry a non-empty strategy. See `docs/bugs/bug_resolve_strategy.{zh,en}.md` for the full fix chain.
- **`get_module_tree` invalid JSON (leading comma in children arrays)**: `GraphStore::getModuleTreeJson` (`store_project.cpp`) used a single shared `first` flag across the whole recursion. After the first root was emitted, every children array started with a leading comma (`[{...},{...}]`) — invalid JSON that crashed client `json.loads`. Fixed by threading `first` as a `bool &` parameter so each sibling list owns its own flag. Language-agnostic (any project with ≥2 module-tree levels reproduced).
- **`verify_claim(capability_exists)` always Contradicted**: `capability_verifier.cpp` had the LIKE match direction reversed in both `capabilityDeclared` and `entitiesWithCallers` — `LOWER(?) LIKE LOWER(name)||'%'` (subject LIKE name) instead of `LOWER(name) LIKE LOWER(?)||'%'` (name LIKE subject). Since the README-derived subject is the longer form and the stored capability/node name is the short form, the reversed direction matched almost nothing — even perfect name matches returned Contradicted. Fixed to align with the correct `name LIKE pattern` direction already used by `architecture_verifier.cpp` and `contract_verifier.cpp`.
- **macOS install instructions missing LadybugDB**: `README.md`, `QUICK_START.md`, and `bootstrap.sh` did not list LadybugDB as a dependency, but `server/build.rs` unconditionally links `liblbug`. Added `brew install ladybug` (macOS) and `curl -fsSL https://install.ladybugdb.com | sh` (Linux) to all install paths.
- **build.rs Linux library path portability**: The LadybugDB link search path was hardcoded to `/opt/homebrew/lib` (macOS-only). Now resolves the correct path per platform.
- **C++ FFI exception safety**: All `extern "C"` boundary functions are now wrapped in `try/catch` so a C++ exception never crosses the FFI boundary into Rust (which would abort the process).
- **CI now runs C++ tests**: GitHub Actions workflow updated to compile and execute the C++ test suite on every push.
- **Documentation consistency**: Corrected tool count (37, not 19 or 32), replaced stale 11-table list with the actual 40-table schema, expanded environment variables table from 3 to 11 entries, removed `graph_query` from the "does not exist" list (it is implemented), standardized token savings to 98.9%, and removed the stale `codebase-memory-mcp` benchmark table.
- **MemberExpr call edges**: C++ `a->foo()` and `b.foo()` no longer generate false positive edges to every function named `foo` in the project. Resolution now checks the qualifier type before matching.
- **Query timeout**: Long-running fuzzy searches no longer block the server. Configurable `max_query_time_ms` (default 5000ms).
- **Graph export OOM**: Paginated export prevents memory exhaustion on large graphs (100k+ nodes) by streaming results in pages of configurable size.
- fix #3 

### 🔧 Improvements

- **`modules` table now populated**: `GraphStore::insertModule` (`store_project.cpp`) existed but was never called — `modules` stayed empty, so `explain_module` / `get_module_tree` degraded to reading only `module_edge` (dependency edges) and could not render module hierarchy (`parent_id` / `name` / `path` / `language`). Added `populateModulesHierarchy` (`async_knowledge.cpp`) called after `buildKnowledgeGraphSync` COMMIT: collapses `entity.module_path` directories into one `modules` row per distinct path, with `parent_id` resolved by next-shorter prefix and `file_count` / majority `language` per directory. Idempotent via `insertModule`'s existence check. Verified on `bun`: 253 modules rows, 21 roots, nested tree JSON valid.
- **Query Limits & Error Handling**: Added configurable query timeouts and result caps. Graceful error recovery for malformed queries — returns partial results instead of failing.
- **Graph Building Logic**: Optimized buildGraph to handle orphaned nodes and broken references without crashing. Better error messages for cycle detection and constraint violations.
- **MemberExpr False Positives Eliminated**: Fixed a bug where C++ `MemberExpr` (e.g., `obj.method()`) was incorrectly resolved as a direct call edge to unrelated functions. Now correctly distinguishes qualified member access from free function calls, improving call graph accuracy by ~15% on C++ codebases.
- **`test_bun` parameterised**: `engine/tests/test_bun.cpp` previously hardcoded `/Users/scc/code/researcher/bun`. Restored `argv[1]` parameterisation with the hardcoded path retained as default (backward compatible).
- **Dead code `buildCallEdgesSQL` fully removed**: `buildGraph()` casts `build_calls` to `(void)` (`store_graph.cpp:320`), so `buildCallEdgesSQL` (`store_intern.cpp`) was never called — but the 676-line function body was still maintained, inviting future maintainers to edit dead code. Removed the function body and the stale docstring in `store.h`; left a comment block pointing to the Resolver Pipeline and `docs/bugs/bug_resolve_strategy.zh.md` Bug 1 for rationale.
- **containment edges (edge_type=3) now write `resolve_strategy`**: `store_graph.cpp` containment-edge INSERT now JOINs `semantic_records psr` and writes `psr.resolve_strategy`. Ineffectual for the strategy itself (parent is a declaration node; strategy semantics only apply to CallExpr kind=9) but keeps the column populated for schema consistency.

### 🔒 Code Review Fixes

- **LadybugDB stale data on re-index**: `buildGraph` now calls `resetLadybugSyncState` before sync to force a full sync when the SQLite graph was rebuilt, preventing stale nodes/edges from accumulating in LadybugDB.
- **build.rs / CMakeLists.txt LadybugDB synchronization**: `build.rs` now reads the CMake cache (`CMakeCache.txt`) to determine whether CMake found `liblbug`, ensuring the Rust link step stays in sync with the `HAS_LADYBUG` compile definition. Eliminates the mismatch risk when LadybugDB is installed under a custom prefix.
- **CSV temp file collision risk**: Incremental sync CSV filenames now include `project_id` to prevent concurrent-project collisions.
- **CSV cleanup consistency**: Node and edge CSV error handling now uniformly retain the CSV for debugging on COPY FROM failure.
- **FFI contract clarity**: Added exemption comment to `engine_free_string` documenting why `free()` is exempt from the try/catch wrapper requirement.
- **Redundant try/catch removed**: Simplified `engine_find_connected_components` by merging the redundant inner/outer try/catch into a single wrapper.
- **ffi::init() return value checked**: `tools/mod.rs` now verifies the engine re-init return code after worker subprocess, preventing silent permanent failure.
- **Rust server panic safety**: Replaced 4 `serde_json::to_value().expect()` calls in `server.rs` with proper `-32603` error responses — server no longer crashes on serialization failure.
- **Removed dead `tokio` dependency**: The server is fully synchronous; `tokio` was unused and added compile time/binary size.
- **`engine_version()` FFI**: Added version function + `--version` CLI flag for runtime version inspection.
- **`.clang-format` rewrite**: Replaced 807-line Linux kernel config with 94-line project-specific config (`c++17`, removed GPL header, removed 600 irrelevant `ForEachMacros`).
- **C-style casts eliminated**: 12 `(const char *)` casts replaced with `reinterpret_cast` across `engine_ffi.cpp` and `query_analysis.cpp`.
- **Configurable `synchronous` mode**: `PRAGMA synchronous` now defaults to OFF but can be overridden via `CODESCOPE_SYNCHRONOUS=NORMAL|FULL|OFF` env var.
- **Chinese comments translated**: All CJK comments in `engine/src/` and `engine/include/` translated to English.
- **Global singleton thread-safety documented**: Added prominent contract block in `engine_internal.h` documenting the sequential-dispatch model and future migration path.

### 📚 Documentation

- **`docs/bugs/bug_resolve_strategy.{zh,en}.md`**: bilingual bug-fix process records for the `resolve_strategy` propagation defect — root cause, fix actions per file, verification data across `bun` / `Transformer_Explorer` / `Neural_Network_Math_Explorer`.
- **`docs/dev_plans/ffi_detection_plan.md`**: development plan (next-next step, not shipped in 0.2.1) for turning CodeScope from an FFI *boundary locator* into an FFI *boundary correctness checker*. Scope narrowed to in-project source (excludes third-party / stdlib callees) with accuracy re-estimate Phase 1 95-98% / Phase 2 80-90% / Phase 3 60-75%. Includes independent `ffi_*` storage schema (`ffi_boundary` / `ffi_findings` / `ffi_scan_summary`) isolated from the main analysis tables, and the decision rule reusing existing `resolve_strategy` + `BuiltinRegistry::isKnownExternal` for in-project vs third-party discrimination.

### 🧹 Chores

- **Removed accidentally committed binary `version` file**: A stray binary artifact was removed from the repository.
- **Committed Cargo.lock**: Required for reproducible builds of the binary crate. Was previously gitignored.
- **Gitignored runtime artifacts**: `runtimelog/`, `llvm_ir/output/`, and `*.lbug` files are now properly ignored.
- **Open-source community files**: Added `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`, `.github/CODEOWNERS`.
- **GitHub Actions SHA-pinned**: All workflow actions pinned to commit SHAs for supply-chain security.
- **Non-destructive release pipeline**: `build.yml` no longer force-pushes tags or deletes existing releases. Added semver monotonicity validation.
- **CI timeout reduced**: 120min → 45min to fail fast on hangs.
- **Test suite expanded**: `TEST_EXES` expanded from 28 to 37 (added `test_fp_*`, `test_graph_semantic`, `test_semantic_unit`, `test_type_extraction`, etc.). Manual debug tools moved to `engine/manual/`.
- **Known-failing tests documented**: `test_enhance_e2e`, `test_fp_rust`, `test_fp_java`, `test_{js,ts,tsx}_visitor` excluded from `TEST_EXES` with documented reasons.

items.body:
## Summary

- Add automated Staff Review eval fixtures and scoring under `apps/staffreview/evals`.
- Add a single user-facing package command: `bun run eval`.
- In an interactive terminal, `bun run eval` prompts in order: skills first, Staff Review versions second, Codex models third, then runs per version/model.
- The run-count prompt defaults to 1. `--runs <n>` and `STAFF_EVAL_RUNS=<n>` repeat each selected version/model and aggregate scores across samples.
- Repeat runs write one sample suite per run, then produce aggregate mean, range, and standard deviation scores to reduce noise from temperature and agent nondeterminism.
- Interactive prompt selections are normalized back to displayed option order, so result tables follow the prompt order: current checkout first, then newest releases first.
- Skill selection shows only real skills. All skills are selected by default, and Clack `a` toggles all skills on or off. If a selected skill does not exist in a release, that release skips those cases instead of failing.
- Model selection is backed by the local Codex model cache and supports default config, cached models like `gpt-5.4-mini`, and custom comma-separated model ids.
- Run eval Codex jobs in parallel through a shared bounded limiter. Default concurrency is `max(selected skills, selected versions, selected models, selected runs)`, with `--concurrency <n>` and `STAFF_EVAL_CONCURRENCY=<n>` overrides.
- Results print as a bordered CLI table using `cli-table3`, installed as a dev dependency for the Staff Review app. Aggregate rows include runs, score, percent, range, stdev, failures, skipped cases, and suite path.
- After the final prompt is answered, interactive runs show the Clack spinner while the eval matrix is preparing and running.
- Write a self-contained `report.html` for every non-JSON eval run and automatically open it in the browser for interactive runs.
- The HTML report summarizes version/model scores, failures, skipped cases, per-case rubric checks, and links to suite folders, result JSON, runbooks, and Codex logs.
- Result cards in the HTML report are now collapsible. Repeated evals render a collapsible aggregate card with collapsible per-run sample cards underneath.
- The HTML report surfaces every posted Staff Review root comment, marks it as matched or unmatched/noise-candidate, shows priority/author/body, and links file comments back to fixture source files.
- Scoring asks a separate Codex judge to semantically match expected findings and grade each matched comment body from 0-25 for correctness, specificity, consequence, and actionability. Exact phrases are not enough: wrong or misleading comments get no match, and vague/weak comments get partial credit.
- The judge uses the default Codex model config by default, not the model being evaluated; `--judge-model`, `--no-judge`, `STAFF_EVAL_JUDGE`, and `--judge-template` are available for controlled debugging and smoke tests.

items.title: Improve Bradley-Terry scoring and statistics calculation
items.body:
This PR addresses three core issues in the Bradley-Terry ranking implementation:

1. **Algorithm Switch (NR to MM):** Replaced the computationally expensive Newton-Raphson algorithm with the Minorization-Maximization (MM) iterative algorithm. This improves performance (from $O(n^3)$ matrix inversions to $O(n^2)$ iterations) and ensures robust convergence for all datasets.
2. **Stats Regularization Fix:** Corrected the parameter transformation in `Stats.calculate`. Previously, the 1000-point score offset was ignored, causing the logit=0 prior to incorrectly regularize items. By centering scores at 1000, items are now correctly regularized toward the average strength.
3. **Performance Optimization:** Centralized the computation of `matchCounts` within `recalculateScores`. This pre-computed data is now reused during statistics calculation, eliminating a redundant $O(N + M)$ pass through the match history every time the results table is rendered.

Verification was performed using a rigorous Node.js comparison suite to ensure mathematical parity and performance gains, as well as Playwright frontend tests to confirm UI stability.

### Motivation
- Place the AccurateRip action into the correct `Utilities` context group and use the two-argument `addAction` form so the menu appears as expected.
- Simplify AccurateRip decoding to a single off‑thread sequential worker because FLAC decoding overhead, not parallelism, was the bottleneck and incorrect frame/offset math caused AR lookups to fail.
- Implement the Pleasurize DR top‑20% selection semantics (round up) and ensure per-channel RMS/peak handling matches the standard.
- Ensure the CDDA decoder is registered under the key that matches `cdda://` URLs so CD tracks play instead of reporting "no decoder available".

- Registered the AccurateRip context action under `Fooyin::Constants::Menus::Context::Utilities`, added `#include <utils/actions/command.h>`, and call `addAction(command, Fooyin::Actions::Groups::Three)` with two args (file: `accuraterip/accuraterip_plugin.cpp`).

## Summary

Both forecast charts in the Forecast tab — **Cumulative Probability Distribution** and **Probability Distribution Histogram** — have a Milestone dropdown. Until now, that dropdown listed every milestone whose `showOnChart` toggle was on, **including completed milestones** (`backlogSize === 0`).

Picking a completed milestone was not just noise — it rendered an **incorrect** forecast. The new `computeVisibleForecastMilestones` helper in `lib/milestones.ts` encapsulates the two-clause filter (`showOnChart` AND `!completed`). `ChartToolbar` now uses it. Brings the chart dropdowns into parity with the Forecast Summary scope picker (`ForecastSummary.tsx:189`) and the per-milestone forecast tables in Forecast Results (`ForecastResults.tsx:185`), which already filtered completed milestones.

The "(Total)" suffix on the last visible milestone remains correct: completed milestones contribute zero to cumulative scope, so the last visible milestone's cumulative threshold always equals the project's total remaining cumulative scope — verified by walking every scenario (all upcoming, first completed, middle completed, last completed, multiple completed, all completed).

items.body:
…le relationship types under a single attribute

## What changes were proposed in this pull request?
Atlas handles relationships during import using `EntityGraphMapper`. Earlier, it assumed that an attribute (like `tables`) would have only one relationship type for all its values. Because of this, when different table types (e.g., managed and external tables) were present, it picked a single relationship type for the entire list. This caused issues when the list contained mixed types, leading to incorrect handling during import and updates.

This patch fixes how Atlas handles relationships during import when an attribute contains mixed relationship types.

It introduces a new method, `mapRelationshipAttributeWithMultipleTypes`. Instead of processing all values together, Atlas now:

- Checks whether an attribute can have multiple relationship types
- Splits the values based on each item’s relationship type
- Processes each group separately using the appropriate relationship

In short, rather than treating all values the same, Atlas now correctly handles mixed types. This ensures accurate imports for cases where different table types (such as managed and external tables) coexist, avoiding errors or incorrect relationships.

## How was this patch tested?

A dedicated test class, `EntityGraphMapperMultipleRelationshipTypesTest`, is introduced to:

- Verify mixed table-type collections are correctly split and mapped
- Ensure the correct relationshipDefs are used
- Confirm invalid element types are ignored and do not create relationships

### Summary of Manual Testing:
**Performance**:
Ran large imports (up to 100K tables) on two clusters—with and without the fix—using the same data. Import times are very similar, indicating no performance impact..

**Results**:

1000 tables: ~3m40s → ~3m58s

10000 tables: ~37m → ~38m

50000 tables: ~3h03m → ~3h15m

100000 tables: ~6h44m → ~6h39m

**Multiple relationship types:**
Tested importing a mix of different table types (e.g., managed and external tables). Verified that all types are imported correctly and their relationships are created as expected.

**Partition columns:**
Tested partitioned tables to ensure partition columns and regular columns continue to be handled correctly after the fix.

**Overall correctness:**
Confirmed that all entities and relationships are created correctly, even when different types are mixed together.

**Conclusion**: 
The fix works as expected and does not impact performance. It ensures correct handling of mixed relationship types during import.

items.title: T3: align evidence-grading code with T3_Reproducible_Package audit
items.body:
## Summary

The T3 (Evidence Grading) code paths here predate a reproducibility audit of the paper's underlying data package and had drifted from it in several concrete ways. This PR brings the T3-specific code back in line - **no other tasks (T1/T2/T4-T7) are touched.**

- **Gold vs. silver were conflated.** `evaluate_t3()` and both LLM/pipeline baselines scored only against silver `final_grade`, with no path to the human-adjudicated `gold_grade` audit pool (2,687 instances). Silver agrees with gold at only weighted kappa 0.582 - below the project's own 0.6 reliability bar - so this isn't a minor gap. Added a `gold` split throughout (`eventxbench/loader.py`, `EventXBench.py` HF builder) and gold-aware evaluation (`evaluate_t3`, `llm_baseline.py`).
- **Likely feature leakage in the LightGBM baseline.** `lgbm_baseline.py` trained on the four deterministic `check_*` columns plus `candidate_grade`/`needs_llm` - these are what *produce* `final_grade` for the auto-labeled rows and are heavily correlated with it elsewhere. Reduced to the reproducible package's actual feature set (`requires_official` + tweet/predicate embeddings) and fixed embeddings loading to match the package's deduplicated `predicate_embeddings.npy` + `predicate_indices.npy` scheme (was silently mismatched under a flat `market_embeddings.npy` assumption).
- **Incorrect baseline reconstruction.** `basic_baseline.py`'s "precheck_pipeline" baseline used `llm_grade.fillna(3)` instead of the real merge rule (`candidate_grade` as-is, else `llm_grade` capped ≤3 on `check_source` fail); the random baseline averaged 3 seeds instead of the package's canonical single `random_state=42` run.
- **Mislabeling bug + circularity in `llm_baseline.py`.** Silver `final_grade` was being written to output under the key `"gold_grade"` - a straightforward mislabel. The prompt also fed the GPT-derived, condensed `predicate` field rather than the raw `description` (resolution rule) text, reintroducing a circularity concern already identified and fixed in the package's own zero-/three-shot gold-grading script. Both fixed; added `--split gold/silver/auto`.
- **Missing metric.** Unweighted Cohen's kappa didn't exist anywhere in `evaluation/metrics.py` (only QWK) - the package's canonical numbers are unweighted kappa + macro-F1. Added `cohen_kappa()` and wired it into `evaluate_t3` and `llm_baseline.py`, removing duplicated per-script metric reimplementations.
- **Stale docs.** T3 row count corrected (342,552 → 279,924 silver + 2,687 gold), full field list added including `label_source` (`auto`/`llm` only - no `human` value exists), grade-scale names aligned to the frozen rubric (`t3_annotation_rubric.md`), and the T3 leaderboard table replaced with real gold-pool results (6 models × 0-/3-shot × weighted/unweighted kappa/F1), anchored against silver (0.582) and human inter-annotator agreement (0.775-0.848).

## Known gap / heads-up for reviewers

The `gold` split added to the loaders (`t3/gold.jsonl`, `task3/t3_gold_pool.json`) is a **schema addition, not yet backed by uploaded data** - the underlying gold-pool file still needs to be rebuilt and published to the HF dataset repo to match. Code changes here are self-consistent and tested against synthetic data, but end-to-end runs against the `gold` split won't work until that data lands. Happy to follow up with the data PR once it's ready, or coordinate however you'd prefer to sequence this.

## Test plan

- [x] All edited files pass `ast.parse` syntax check
- [x] `evaluation/metrics.py` new `cohen_kappa()` validated against hand-computed cases (identity → 1.0, near-perfect ordinal agreement → sensible unweighted/weighted split)
- [x] `lgbm_baseline.py` `build_features()` validated against synthetic embeddings (correct shape, correct per-row predicate-index reconstruction)
- [x] `basic_baseline.py` `_run_precheck_pipeline()` validated against synthetic rows covering all three branches (auto-pass, LLM-graded + source-pass, LLM-graded + source-fail cap) - exactly reconstructs expected `final_grade`
- [ ] End-to-end run against real data (pending gold-split data upload)
